comment:
* SIP Stack extensions to be added to the next spec revision. Only these may be safely used in * the interim between now and the next release. SipStackImpl implements this interface. * * The following new stack initialization flags are defined (not the gov.nist prefix will be * dropped when the spec is updated): * *
    *
  • gov.nist.javax.sip.AUTOMATIC_DIALOG_ERROR_HANDLING *
  • gov.nist.javax.sip.IS_BACK_TO_BACK_USER_AGENT *
  • gov.nist.javax.sip.DELIVER_TERMINATED_EVENT_FOR_NULL_DIALOG *
  • gov.nist.javax.sip.MAX_FORK_TIME_SECONDS *
* @author M. Ranganathan *

methods.name: public void setAddressResolver(AddressResolver addressResolver)
methods.comment:
* Set the address resolution interface. The address resolver allows you to register custom
     * lookup schemes ( for example DNS SRV lookup ) that are not directly supported by the JDK.
     *
     * @param addressResolver -- the address resolver to set.
     *
     * @since 2.0

methods.comment: * Get the dialog in the Join header. * * @return Dialog object matching the Join header, provided it is in an appropriate state to * be replaced, null otherwise * * @since 2.0

methods.name: public void setEnabledCipherSuites(String[] newCipherSuites)
methods.comment:
* Set the list of cipher suites supported by the stack. A stack can have only one set of * suites. These are not validated against the supported cipher suites of the java runtime, so * specifying a cipher here does not guarantee that it will work.
* The stack has a default cipher suite of: *
    *
  • TLS_RSA_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA
    • *
  • SSL_RSA_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA
    • *
  • TLS_DH_anon_WITH_AES_128_CBC_SHA
    • *
  • SSL_DH_anon_WITH_3DES_EDE_CBC_SHA
    • *
* * NOTE: This function must be called before adding a TLS listener * * @since 2.0 * @param newCipherSuites -- The new set of ciphers to support. *

methods.name: public SocketAddress obtainLocalAddress(InetAddress dst, int dstPort, InetAddress localAddress, int localPort) throws IOException
methods.comment:
* Creates and binds, if necessary, a TCP socket connected to the specified
     * destination address and port and then returns its local address.
     *
     * @param dst the destination address that the socket would need to connect
     *            to.
     * @param dstPort the port number that the connection would be established
     * with.
     * @param localAddress the address that we would like to bind on
     * (null for the "any" address).
     * @param localPort the port that we'd like our socket to bind to (0 for a
     * random port).
     *
     * @return the SocketAddress that this handler would use when connecting to
     * the specified destination address and port.
     *
     * @throws IOException
